title: Center a benchtop balance's bubble with its two leveling feet
instruction: Use the two front leveling wheels to center the bubble on the balance. Then move both grippers away and leave the balance resting on its feet.
context: Before weighing reagents or samples, lab technicians level the balance to keep readings repeatable. They use the round vial to correct two axes. Extending both front feet raises the front, and extending one relative to the other rolls the case sideways.
setup: An empty 2.2 kg precision balance, polymer housing 221 × 179 mm and stainless pan 144 × 153 mm, sits loose on a horizontal bench. Its two knurled steel thumbscrew wheels are 45 mm across and their rubber pads are 236 mm apart. The fixed rear rubber foot is 203 mm behind their line. The left and right pads start 3.1 and 5.4 mm higher than the rear pad in the balance frame. All three bear on the bench when it settles. A 27 mm green bullseye vial sits beside the front display. Both grippers start open and clear.
scoring: Check that all three feet are bearing on the bench and that both grippers have withdrawn. 1.0 if the entire bubble fits inside the inner ring and the balance stays still there for 2 seconds. 0.5 if the bubble center is within 3 mm of the rings' center on a still, unsupported-by-hands balance. Otherwise 0. Use a close overhead video of the vial and side footage of the three feet and both hands. In simulation, full credit also checks an absolute pitch and roll combination within 0.16 degrees.
reset_notes: Empty the pan and set the balance down with the fixed rear foot and both adjustable pads bearing on the same bench, with the initial height offsets restored. Wait for the bubble to settle off center.
fidelity: Each wheel has a contact-driven revolute joint. Its measured rotation maps through a 3 mm screw pitch to a load-bearing prismatic pad. The balance tips freely on the three contacts. Two orthogonal slides represent the vial bubble following gravity, with damping. Screw threads and the fluid surface are approximated.
scores: Dream-1: 0.0 at the 1,200-step limit. Scripted demo: 1.0 at step 940 (47.0 simulated seconds); final tilt 0.10°, bubble center offset 0.61 mm. Single-foot control: 0.0.
